_about: Plain-language definitions shown in the info-icon tooltips. Keys are referenced from components (Info term=...).

perfect_foresight.definition: Each day's charge and discharge schedule is chosen with that day's real-time prices already known. No real operator can do this, so it is a ceiling on energy arbitrage, not a forecast.

capture_rate.definition: Revenue from scheduling on day-ahead prices (and being paid real-time prices) divided by the perfect-foresight revenue for the same battery and days. 70% means the realistic strategy kept 70 cents of every perfect-foresight dollar.

usd_per_kw_yr.definition: Dollars earned per year for each kilowatt of power capacity. Because it is per kW, a 10 MW and a 100 MW battery with the same duration have the same figure. 2026 values are scaled up from year-to-date to 365 days.

usd_per_kwh_yr.definition: Dollars earned per year for each kilowatt-hour of energy capacity. Equals $/kW-yr divided by the duration in hours, so it shows how well each hour of storage is used.

cycles.definition: Full-capacity equivalents per year: total energy discharged divided by the battery's energy capacity. Two half-depth discharges count as one cycle.

spread_captured.definition: Average price the battery sold at minus the average price it bought at, weighted by energy, in $/MWh. Efficiency losses and degradation cost come out of this spread.

hub.definition: An ERCOT trading hub: an average price over many nodes in a region (Houston, North, South, West, Panhandle). Hubs are a smooth reference price; no battery sits at a hub.

resource_node.definition: The settlement point where one generator or battery is paid. Its price includes local grid congestion, so it can differ a lot from the hub and spike more often.

load_zone.definition: An ERCOT region whose customers pay one averaged price (for example LZ_WEST). Here each resource node is matched to the hub of its load zone for comparison.

da.definition: The day-ahead market, cleared the day before for each hour. A strategy that is "DA-scheduled" plans its charge and discharge from these prices, then is paid real-time prices.

rt.definition: The real-time market, with prices every 15 minutes (settlement point prices). Most of the revenue in this model is earned and measured at these prices.

rtcb.definition: Real-Time Co-optimization plus Batteries, an ERCOT market redesign that went live on Dec 5, 2025. It buys energy and ancillary services together every few minutes and changes how battery revenue is earned.

degradation_cost.definition: A charge per MWh discharged ($0 or $10 here) standing in for battery wear. Revenue shown is net of it, and it makes the optimizer skip trades that are too thin to be worth the wear.

top10_day_share.definition: The share of the period's total revenue earned on its ten best days. A high share means the result depends on a few price spikes.

corr_hub.definition: How closely a node's 15-minute real-time price moves with its load zone's trading hub over the year (1 = moves exactly together). Low values mean local congestion often pulls the node's price away from the hub.

quantile_scale.definition: Nodes are sorted by $/kW-yr and split into classes holding about the same number of nodes each, so every colour is used equally. Class edges are uneven in dollars because a few nodes earn far more than the rest.

installed_cost.definition: All-in upfront cost to build the battery, per kWh of energy capacity: cells, inverters, civil work, interconnection and development. A 2-hour battery at $300/kWh costs $600 per kW of power. Quotes vary widely by year and scope, so treat the default as a placeholder.

fixed_om.definition: Yearly operations and maintenance cost that does not depend on how much the battery runs: monitoring, site upkeep, insurance, warranty and service contracts. Per kW of power capacity.

augmentation.definition: Cells fade with use, so owners often add battery modules part-way through the project to restore capacity. Modeled here as one payment, in dollars per kWh of energy capacity, at the end of the year you choose.

project_life.definition: Years of operation counted in the cash flows. Nothing is earned after this, and no resale value is assumed.

discount_rate.definition: The yearly return you require; future dollars are shrunk by it to get today's value. Higher rates punish projects that earn their money late. Real (no inflation) terms, matching the model.

itc.definition: A share of the installed cost returned through the tax system. It is your input: this site does not encode any tax law, and eligibility, rate and timing depend on the project. Modeled as a reduction of the year-0 outlay.

revenue_haircut.definition: A cut applied to the modeled revenue to move away from perfect foresight toward what an operator might actually earn (forecast error, outages, bidding limits, unmodeled costs). 30% means you keep 70% of the modeled revenue.

revenue_decline.definition: How much revenue shrinks each year, as a percentage of the prior year. It stands in for price spreads narrowing as more batteries arrive, plus capacity fade. 3% a year compounds to about 46% lower by year 20.

npv.definition: Every year's cash flow shrunk to today's dollars at the discount rate, then added up, minus the upfront cost. Above zero means the project earns more than the required return. Shown per kW of power capacity.

irr.definition: The discount rate at which NPV is exactly zero: the project's own yearly return. Compare it with your required return. Shown as 'none' when the project never earns back its cost.

payback.definition: Years until cumulative cash flow, with no discounting, gets back the upfront cost. Ignores everything after that point and ignores the time value of money.

lcos.definition: The break-even price: all lifetime costs (upfront, O&M, augmentation) in today's dollars divided by the MWh the battery discharges, also in discounted terms. Charging electricity is not included because the revenue is already net of it.

breakeven_capex.definition: The installed cost per kWh at which NPV is exactly zero, holding every other input fixed. If real quotes are below it, the project clears your required return under these assumptions.

tornado.definition: Each input is moved down and up by a fixed step while the rest stay put, and the bar shows how far NPV moves. Longest bars are the inputs that matter most. It does not show combinations of changes.

ancillary_services.definition: Capacity held ready to help balance the grid. Regulation Up and Down manage frequency; Responsive Reserve (RRS), ECRS and Non-Spin provide upward reserves. Capacity is paid per MW-hour, separately from energy delivered. This screen reserves shared battery power and energy, but does not simulate actual AS activation.
